Note::replace¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::replace(std::string_view from, std::string_view to) const

Substitute Every Occurrence Of A Literal Substring¶

replace(from, to) returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with every occurrence of the literal string from in each cell rewritten to to. Despite the bare name, this is a replace-all: it is the workhorse for normalizing separators, renaming a token throughout a batch, or swapping placeholder text.

The match is literal — from is compared byte for byte, no regex metacharacters, no case folding. Occurrences are rewritten left to right and non-overlapping, and the scan resumes after the inserted to (not inside it), so a to that contains from does not cause a second pass: replace("aa", "b") on "aaaa" gives "bb".

Edge cases¶

  • An empty from is a no-op — the cell is returned unchanged (not an error, and not “insert to between every character”).

  • An empty to deletes every from; that is exactly remove_all(from).

  • No occurrence of from leaves the cell unchanged.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. For “first only” or “last only” or “first N”, use the sibling methods replace_first, replace_last, and replace_n.

Example 1: Every Occurrence Is Rewritten¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"score: 75 score: x", "pending"}).replace("score", "mark"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["mark: 75 mark: x", "pending"]

Both scores in the first cell change; the second cell has none and is unchanged.

Example 2: Normalize A Separator¶

const pluss::Note n =
    pluss::make_note({"Ada_Lovelace", "Grace_Hopper"}).replace("_", " ");
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["Ada Lovelace", "Grace Hopper"]

Example 3: Matches Do Not Overlap And The Result Is Not Re-Scanned¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout, pluss::make_note({"aaaa"}).replace("aa", "b"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["bb"]

Example 4: An Empty from Is A No-Op¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::make_note({"unchanged"}).replace("", "X"))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["unchanged"]

Example 5: An Empty to Deletes — Same As remove_all¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::make_note({"a.b.c"}).replace(".", ""))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["abc"]

Example 6: Shape Is Preserved¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({{"x1", "x2"}, {"x3", "x4"}}).replace("x", "col"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["col1", "col2"], 
  ["col3", "col4"]
]

See Also¶

  • Note::remove_all: replace(from, "") — delete every occurrence.

  • pluss::coden::Note::replace_first / replace_last / replace_n: bounded substitution instead of replace-all.

  • Note::RegexAccessor::findall: when the target is a pattern, not a fixed string.
